The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: 240 {A1} of 240 {A2} shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31 {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-04T04:00:00Z {A4}. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 {A5} days, so the fault is up to that old.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T04:00:13Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T04:00:15Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 7 days 13 seconds {alerted_after_the_onset} after the onset.
Broken from 2026-11-04T04:00:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T04:00:58Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 7 days 58 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 44 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T04:00:58Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - metrics were read, but none from the hour before the onset, so there is no calm level to measure a rise against.
Customer loss: none so far - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What each deployment it looked into changed:
  - [D1] Deployment of revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 to io-shop, compared against 4c810f22894e612ced87f5ee3f3062dfeb785050 - the revision deployed before it.
      modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py
        @@ -28,26 +28,23 @@
         
         
         def record_purchase(account: Account, purchase: Purchase) -> Account:
        -    """The account with this purchase written into it, and both totals moved.
        +    """The account with this purchase written into it, and its total moved.
         
        -    How a purchase has always been recorded. Each total is added to rather than
        -    worked out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale
        -    changes it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
        +    How a purchase is recorded. The lifetime total is added to rather than worked
        +    out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale changes
        +    it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
         
        -    The month is the part worth reading twice. A purchase counts towards the
        -    month's total only if it falls in the month being counted, so that addition is
        -    conditional where the lifetime one is not - and a shopper backfilling an older
        -    order leaves this month's figure exactly where it was.
        +    The month is no longer carried. Every purchase says whether it falls in the
        +    current month, so what a shopper has spent this month adds up from the history
        +    whenever anybody wants it - exactly as the lifetime average is derived from the
        +    purchases rather than read off the account. A second copy of a figure the
        +    purchases already hold is a copy that has to be kept in step, and the cheapest
        +    way to keep it in step is not to keep it.
             """
             return replace(
                 account,
                 purchases=(*account.purchases, purchase),
        -        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents,
        -        total_this_month_cents=(
        -            account.total_this_month_cents + purchase.price_cents
        -            if purchase.in_current_month
        -            else account.total_this_month_cents
        -        )
        +        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents
             )
         
         
  - A file [D1] does not list is as it was at the revision [D1] compares against.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] Which code each claim is about:
      - The deployed revision 26f1d7e2 is not in main's history, so I have not read it. The claim that it removed the total_this_month_cents update from `record_purchase` comes from the investigation's deploy diff, not from code I saw.
      - On main, in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py, `record_purchase` still moves `total_this_month_cents`. But main has the same fault in `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which `record_a_purchase` calls when `derive_the_month` is true. That function adds the purchase and moves `total_cents`, but copies `total_this_month_cents` across unchanged. That is the same omission the investigation describes in the deployed revision. So turning that path on, or deploying the branch again, would leave stored month totals out of line with the purchases again.
      
      The fix, in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: `record_purchase_deriving_the_month` now sets `total_this_month_cents` to the sum of `price_cents` over the account's purchases (including the new one) where `in_current_month` is true. So the path writes the month total it derives instead of dropping it. An account with a total that has already drifted gets the correct figure the next time it is written through this path. `record_purchase` and `record_a_purchase` are unchanged, and the field keeps its name and type.
      
      Tests (tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py): three new cases. They assert that the deriving path, called directly and through `record_a_purchase(..., derive_the_month=True)`, leaves `total_this_month_cents` equal to the sum of this month's purchase prices. One case also asserts that `reconcile_monthly_totals` reports nothing for the result. Against main as it stands, they are written to fail, because the deriving path returns the account's old month total. Nothing has run them.
      
      Repair (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py): the patch only prevents new wrong totals. It does not fix the ones already written. This one-off script reads accounts as JSON lines. It passes them to `reconcile_monthly_totals` and takes the shopper ids that come back as disagreeing. For those accounts only, it sets `total_this_month_cents` to the sum of this month's purchase prices and leaves every other field of the input line as it was. It is a dry run unless `--apply` is passed, in which case it writes only the corrected accounts. Either way it prints how many accounts it checked and changed. The JSON-lines format is my assumption, since I don't know how the store exports or loads accounts: whoever runs it has to export the accounts in that shape and load the corrected ones back. **The script has not been run. A person has to run it**, ideally after this fix is deployed and before the month rolls over, because `in_current_month` is what it sums by.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'. [F1] was written against main, which does not contain the revision running when the alert fired: merged, its fix changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. [F1] names tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py on main as it was at 26f1d7e, which ran. What [F1] says of that file holds for what ran; what it says of the rest of main does not. [F1] names revision 26f1d7e2 and [D1] is that revision's own diff - say what it shows rather than ask for it to be checked.

What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired:
  - [S1] src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py at 26f1d7e
      """Writing a purchase down - the other side of what the account page reads.
      
      An account carries two running totals beside its purchases: what the shopper has
      spent altogether, and what they have spent this month. Recording a sale means
      writing the purchase and moving both of them, and this is where that happens.
      
      Running totals rather than figures derived on demand, because that is what they
      are for. The account page is the most-visited page the shop has and a history is
      long; a total that was summed on every render would make every page pay for the
      whole of a shopper's past. What that buys costs something in return, and the cost
      is the only thing worth knowing about this module: a total is a second copy of
      what the purchases already say, so a write that moves one and not the other leaves
      the shop holding two answers to the same question. Nothing here notices if that
      happens - see `io_shop.spend_reconciliation`, which is the shop's own check on
      exactly this.
      
      Which path a purchase is recorded through arrives here already decided, exactly
      as the choice of figure does on the read side - see `io_shop.spend_summary`.
      Nothing in this module reads a flag, and nothing in it knows a rollout is
      happening.
      """
      
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import replace
      
      from io_shop.accounts import Account, Purchase
      
      
      def record_purchase(account: Account, purchase: Purchase) -> Account:
          """The account with this purchase written into it, and its total moved.
      
          How a purchase is recorded. The lifetime total is added to rather than worked
          out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale changes
          it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
      
          The month is no longer carried. Every purchase says whether it falls in the
          current month, so what a shopper has spent this month adds up from the history
          whenever anybody wants it - exactly as the lifetime average is derived from the
          purchases rather than read off the account. A second copy of a figure the
          purchases already hold is a copy that has to be kept in step, and the cheapest
          way to keep it in step is not to keep it.
          """
          return replace(
              account,
              purchases=(*account.purchases, purchase),
              total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents
          )
      
      
      def record_purchase_deriving_the_month(account: Account,
                                             purchase: Purchase) -> Account:
          """The same account, without the month's total being moved.
      
          One total to carry instead of two, which is the saving: a month is not
          something the shop has to keep a figure for. Every purchase says which month
          it falls in, so what a shopper has spent this month adds up from the history
          whenever anybody wants it - exactly as the lifetime average is derived from the
          purchases rather than read off the account (see
          `io_shop.spend_summary.average_spend_per_item`). Keeping a second copy of a
          figure the purchases already hold is the work this path exists to drop.
          """
          return replace(
              account,
              purchases=(*account.purchases, purchase),
              total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents
          )
      
      
      def record_a_purchase(account: Account,
                            purchase: Purchase,
                            derive_the_month: bool) -> Account:
          """The account this purchase leaves behind, written through whichever path
          the rollout selects.
      
          The decision arrives made, like every other rollout decision in this shop:
          whoever handled the sale was told by the flag SDK which cohort this shopper
          is in, and hands the answer down. A write path that evaluated a flag for
          itself would be a second place the rollout is decided, and the two would
          eventually disagree about which shoppers are in it.
          """
          if derive_the_month:
              return record_purchase_deriving_the_month(account, purchase)
      
          return record_purchase(account, purchase)
      

How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus:
  - [U1] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
  - [U2] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
  - [U3] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
  - [U4] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
  - [U5] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
  - [U6] total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
  - Where [F1] says otherwise of these lines, they stand. src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py, src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py and src/io_shop/spend_summary.py are on main as they were at 26f1d7e, which ran: what these lines say of them holds for what ran.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
  - AI-2 (mitigate, open): Roll io-shop back
Rewriting what the incident wrote wrong is left to a person by design: say it in still_at_risk and the action items, never under went_wrong.
PR #554 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P2] - suspected, not confirmed.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The change removed the line in record_purchase that added each in-month purchase's price to the account's stored total_this_month_cents, on the reasoning that the month could be derived from the purchase history, yet left the stored field in place. The monthly statement still reads that field as the month total and divides it by the number of purchases to get the mean, the spend summary divides it by the number of this month's purchases, and the reconciliation check compares it with the sum of this month's purchase prices. So every purchase recorded afterwards left the stored figure further behind the purchases.
cause_in_plain_words: A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.
still_at_risk: Every purchase recorded through either write path on the running revision could keep leaving shoppers' stored monthly totals short, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong in the monthly statements and spend figures that read them until someone rewrites them.
symptom: Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' stored monthly spend totals no longer matched the purchases behind them: each affected total came out short of what the shopper had bought this month. (cites AL1)
causal_chain 2: Purchases recorded on the running code were added to the account and to the lifetime total, but the stored this-month total was left where it was. The reconciliation check compares that stored figure with the sum of the in-month purchases, so it found the stored figure short. (cites S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired"; U4, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U5, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus")
causal_chain 3: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, removed the update to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed"; T11, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, which is after the later deploy at {P2.1}. (cites AL1; P1, under "Changes to production it read"; P2, under "Changes to production it read")
causal_chain 4: The change stopped keeping the month total on the reasoning that it could be derived from the history, but it left the stored field in place, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read that stored field. (cites D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed"; S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired"; U1, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U2, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U3, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U4, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U5, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; U6, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus")
contributing_factors 1: The only thing that found the drift was the spend-integrity check, which runs once every {A5} days. No more frequent check was seen comparing stored monthly totals with the purchases behind them.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran more often would have caught the wrong totals soon after the deploy, so far fewer totals would have been written wrong before anyone knew.
contributing_factors 2: Before the change was deployed, no check was seen that records purchases through the ledger's write paths and confirms the stored monthly total still matches the purchases.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have failed on a change that stopped moving the month total, and the change would have been held back before it reached production.
action_items 1: Export the accounts and run Code-Fix's repair script against them (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py), first as a dry run and then with --apply, and load the corrected accounts back. Do this once a revision that maintains the month total is running, and before the month rolls over.
action_items 2: Run the spend-integrity check that compares stored monthly totals with the purchases far more often than it runs now.
action_items 3: Add a test that runs for every change to the purchase ledger. It should record purchases through each write path (record_purchase, record_purchase_deriving_the_month and record_a_purchase both ways) and assert that reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing for the result.
action_items 4: Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended waited on a person noticing it.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.
